title: "TSV · AEDT model inspection"

These examples first build an inspectable AEDT model. They answer a concrete
question: are the face conductors, hollow TSV walls, perforated substrate and
electrical assignments represented as intended before a solver setup is chosen?
OrPen owns the layouts and canonical notebooks; SCGSim supplies the reusable
preparation, native transaction and returned-model reader.

## System and representation

- **Concentric system:** annular Signal pads on both die faces connect through
  the central hollow TSV. Four surrounding TSVs connect the two separate Ground
  planes. The Signal opening and bore are not Ground.
- **Ground-stitched CPW:** a through Signal reaches the two exterior cuts; two
  rows of TSVs stitch top and back Ground. It is a full 3D system, not a uniform
  Q2D section or a claim of optimal TSV spacing.
- **Model:** face metal/landings use Thin Film. Hollow TiN walls and cut Silicon
  remain finite Solid. The physical source thickness and material identity stay
  recorded; the backend handles declared source-to-effective Z mapping.

The canonical factories in `orpen_sc_pdk.cells.simulation.scgsim.tsv` own shapes,
holes, source occurrences and contact intent. Concrete dimensions,
Net membership and enclosure controls live in each notebook.

their own declared checkpoints and historical evidence.

## Workflow and expected output

1. Build the canonical layout and inspect detached source facts.
2. Adopt the notebook's explicit Nets and model representation, then prepare a
   fresh handoff. This is source/backend input preparation, not a native model.
3. Select the explicit native **Prepare Only** action to build, read back, save
   and release the model. No Analysis Setup or sweep is created.
4. Use `resolve_prepared_model` in a fresh kernel to inspect the returned model
   and its actual `.aedt` identity without rebuilding it.

Inspect the actual body/sheet and assignment records, together with the saved
project and necessary unsolved companions. Preserve inconclusive contact or
boundary queries as unknown. Keep writable Human inspection copies separate
from hash-bound producer files.

::: {.callout-note title="Model inspection, not a solve result"}
There is no C/G matrix, eigenfrequency, S-data, field or EPR result in this
stage. Source contacts and a saved model do not prove native electrical
continuity or numerical accuracy. Future solve settings are a separate task.
:::

These canonical sources and clean notebooks are a local **CONVERGING**
candidate. Rendering them does not execute their cells; older Solid models are
not outputs of the current mixed Thin Film/Solid examples.
